title: Case: Bulky delivery requires the recipient to clear an access route
context: A two-person furniture crew has supplied an access checklist. The customer must confirm it before the crew retains the booking.
initial_request:
I have put the small shoes away but I have not confirmed the access requirements. Can you keep the delivery booking for 2027-02-10?

If this is not sorted by Friday I am instructing my solicitor and reporting you to Trading Standards.

events.from: Furniture delivery team, Marrowby Arc Logistics
events.body: DL-1345 is a boxed armchair, 82 cm wide. Our accepted booking needs a clear route with at least 90 cm usable width, no loose obstacles and no unreported stairs. This is our crew’s checklist, not advice to move heavy furniture yourself.

I have put the small shoes away but I have not confirmed the access requirements. Can you keep the delivery booking for 2027-02-10?

If this is not sorted by Friday I am instructing my solicitor and reporting you to Trading Standards.

must: Hands the case to a human supervisor with the facts, including the legal threat
must_not: Admits fault or liability, or offers compensation
Sends the customer a message that commits the desk to an outcome, date or payment
Customer measurements support planning, not a guarantee of safe unloading on arrival.

rationale: Rule-made from delivery-009: people, organisations and references renamed, dates moved 364 days. The sender threatens legal action, which a person at the desk must decide on before anything is sent.
